methodological_rigor.justification: The study combines 20 newly sequenced TETs (WES, RNA-seq, WGS) with 117 TCGA cases (total 137 TETs: 124 thymomas, 13 thymic carcinomas), murine TEC scRNA-seq from developmental timepoints including newly generated data from 11-week FVB thymi (1,791 cells after QC), and published scRNA-seq and spatial transcriptomics from 9 additional TET samples. Analytical methods are appropriate and rigorous: BWA-MEM/GATK/VarScan2/Strelka2 for somatic calling, Sequenza with pathology-informed purity correction, COSMIC signature fitting, RNA velocity, BBKNN batch correction, one-class logistic regression (gelnet) for cell-of-origin inference, and an explicit amplification-timing EM decomposition. Survival analyses use Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards with relevant covariates (sex, Masaoka stage, GTF2I/IRS4). Functional validation (IRS4 overexpression, linsitinib/IGF1R inhibition) is modest. Low tumor cell fractions are methodologically handled (RNA-based GTF2I rescue in 16 cases) but limit some inferences.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a molecular characterization study of archival TET samples; Oxford LoE 4 (case series / low-quality cohort with no prospective comparator). Clinical relevance is meaningful because TET histologic classification is known to have poor interobserver reproducibility; the proposed molecular stratification (GTF2I-type, CN-type with IRS4 activation, thymic carcinoma from tuft-like cells) informs prognosis (recurrence-free survival analysis) and nominates IGF1R as a druggable target in CN-type tumors.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE is the closest fit for this observational molecular cohort (hybridized with TCGA). IRB approvals (IRB-1407-063-592 and IRB-19-303), animal protocol (KA2018-40), patient consent, and cohort inclusion dates (November 2010 to May 2014) are stated. Analytical pipelines are specified with tool versions and RRIDs. Clinical endpoints (recurrence-free survival, Masaoka stage) are pre-specified. Use of public TCGA data is noted; however, deposition of the 20 newly generated WES/RNA-seq/WGS datasets and the new murine scRNA-seq is not clearly described in the provided methods.

novelty_literature.justification: The paper advances beyond prior TET genomic landscapes (Petrini 2014, TCGA 2018) by integrating genome, transcriptome, murine single-cell TEC development, and spatial transcriptomics to assign cell-of-origin hypotheses: GTF2I-mutant thymomas resembling TEP progenitors, CN-type thymomas resembling differentiated TECs with IRS4 activation, and thymic carcinomas resembling DCLK1+ tuft cells. The amplification-timing analysis showing early CN alterations in CN-type thymomas and the IRS4 cryptic-exon/APA discovery are novel contributions. Represents a substantial integrative extension rather than a first-in-class discovery.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly organized, with a logical narrative linking genomic subgroups to transcriptomic origins and then to evolutionary timing. Methods are detailed with explicit equations for the amplification-timing model. Figure and table callouts are consistent, and the introduction establishes the clinical problem (poor reproducibility of histologic classification) cleanly. Some methods passages (e.g., wCorr weighting, mini-pseudobulk ranking) are dense but necessary.

key_strengths: Largest integrative WES + RNA-seq + WGS thymic epithelial tumor cohort to date (137 tumors) with three-subgroup molecular classification
Novel cell-of-origin inferences linking each TET subgroup to specific murine TEC developmental states (TEP, differentiated mTEC, tuft cells) via one-class logistic regression
Amplification-timing analysis demonstrates early CN events in CN-type thymomas, supporting distinct evolutionary trajectories
Druggable-target nomination: IRS4 transcriptional activation in CN-type with linsitinib/IGF1R preclinical evidence
key_concerns: Thymic carcinoma subgroup is small (n=13) and originates solely from two-center samples; tuft-cell origin claim rests on limited transcriptomic similarity
Functional validation of IRS4 is confined to HEK293T overexpression; no TET-derived model confirms pathway dependence
Data deposition (accession numbers) for 20 new TET sequencing and newly generated murine scRNA-seq is not clearly reported
Recurrence-free survival analysis is underpowered for overall survival due to event rarity
chief_reviewer.rationale: A methodologically careful integrative multi-omic classification of a rare tumor with clear translational hooks; tier-2 plausible (JCO Precision Oncology / Nature Communications oncology) pending minor revisions on validation and data sharing.
